newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China propaganda organs slam Patten over HK scandal.
newsitem.headline: China propaganda organs slam Patten over HK scandal.

text.p: China's propaganda organs in Hong Kong on Friday hit out at British colonial Governor Chris Patten, Beijing's nemesis, for his handling of a growing political scandal over a top official ousted last July.

"How can someone, who is not chosen by the Hong Kong people, and taking a handsome salary from Hong Kong public coffers while not paying a cent of tax, make judgments on civil servants' integrity?" the China-controlled daily Ta Kung Pao said.

Patten, who infuriated China with his democratic reforms in 1992 and who has sparred constantly with Beijing, on Thursday denied a cover-up and attributed the removal of Immigration Director Laurence Leung to problems of personal integrity.
This version has failed to satisfy many politicians who have asked if there were other reasons for removing Leung last July, possibly a security scandal or a spy case.
Last Friday, Leung, contradicting his and the government's earlier story that he had quit for personal reasons, told the inquiry that he was forced out by the colonial administration.

Ta Kung Pao urged Patten to reveal the whole truth behind what it called the "firing" of Leung and said he was the key to ending the scandal that was rocking the colony only months before it reverts to Chinese rule.
Lashing out at his critics, Patten accused them of minimising the seriousness of the government's charges of improper behaviour by Leung.
The government's personnel chief, Lam Woon-kwong, testified to a Legislative Council inquiry on Wednesday that an anti-graft probe had shown Leung to have undisclosed shareholdings.
It also found he had a business relationship with a legislator, investments in a mainland China enterprise, and had violated rules on repayment of a government housing loan.
Leung's sudden retirement last July stirred an uproar in the territory. British press reports alleged he had been spying for China, which takes over the colony from Britain on July 1.
Leung has denied these allegations and Patten has said Leung never compromised the security of the Immigration Department.
Another Beijing-controlled Hong Kong newspaper, Wen Wei Po, accused Patten of blackening Hong Kong's reputation and that of its Civil Service through the international media.
"Chris Patten is once again spreading negative comments on Hong Kong's future and distorting China's 'one country, two systems' policy," it said.
"With his close ties with British correspondents, one must wonder where all these false allegations are coming from?"
